scope: Four changed files: portable source, generated source, model-choice regression and independent-gate regression.

checks.result: Choice set intersects available controls with actual fixture policy; effectful options require a fixture and explicit allowed operation. Existing non-effectful done/blocked/scroll/observe controls and STOP retain their semantics. Same policy object supplies trusted shared state.
New regression rejects unauthorized fill/press_enter choices in a fixture authorizing fill_submit/check; existing payload, action sequence and safety assertions retained.

Policy-negative test injects an already-formed valid low-risk decision at the ask seam, because the new upstream choice filter otherwise makes unauthorized operations unreachable through normal valid model replies. Independent action gate and browser effects remain real; blocked_policy and acts[] assertions unchanged.
Risk/hold checks, deterministic action_denial, preflight and browser.act order unchanged. web_contract.py has no diff.
Portable and generated source byte-identical and committed together, following documented packaging standards.
No actionable new smell. One policy object is reused; bounded control-set membership is simpler than additional branching or abstraction.

negative_oracle_assessment.why_gate_is_reached: Decision is built using the authorized scenario and actual stub answer validation, with risk0, valid observed e3 target and high-confidence choices. It is then injected while executing safety={} so candidate and origin are valid but effectful policy authorization is absent.
negative_oracle_assessment.what_is_mocked: Only ask, the upstream decision-producing seam. action_denial, browser.preflight, browser.act, result creation and effect list are not mocked.
negative_oracle_assessment.counterfactual: If independent gate authorization were bypassed or permitted this decision, FakeBrowser.act would append fill_submit and mutate todos; unchanged empty-acts and blocked-policy assertions would fail.
negative_oracle_assessment.coverage_split: Normal operation-choice filtering is covered by the new payload regression; policy enforcement against bypassed model/decision selection remains covered by this lower-boundary negative test. Existing invalid-ID and origin checks remain present.

supplied_test_evidence.red: Inspected RED log fails exactly at unauthorized fill/press_enter choice assertion.
supplied_test_evidence.green: Inspected targeted Jev log contains PASS; engine log reports Ran22tests and OK.
supplied_test_evidence.limitation: These logs do not themselves record full argv/exit status; reviewer did not execute implementation/tests or rerun the suite.

limitations: Static Standards review only; no implementation, provider/model/browser, build or test execution by reviewer.
No confidence threshold, budget, fixture authority, local gate or oracle relaxed. Model-choice filtering is defense in depth, not the sole authorization gate.
Full npm and12-case live measurements remain in progress per parent. No live model or whole-issue acceptance is inferred.
All earlier source reviews and failure evidence remain preserved.
